label: copy phase of length-3 sequences (peaks at final output step)
explanation: Never active during the original phase or on the <DEL> step; only active in the copy phase. Strongly selective for the shortest sequences (L=3): in the copy phase of L=3 sequences it is active ~80% of the time and these steps hold ~59% of activation mass. Largest activations are at the last step of L=3 sequences (t=5, recall_idx 2, input = orig(1)): that step alone is active 99.7% of the time and holds ~50% of mass, with top examples near max. t=4 in L=3 is weaker and less reliable. Outside L=3 it fires weakly and sparsely (rate <=3%) in the copy phase of longer sequences, concentrated near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1) and at recall_idx 2 for L=4, plus scattered weak activity in L=9; no clean rule for these was found. Token identity has only modest effect (inputs h, r, 3, f a bit higher). It does not fire on the first occurrence of a token (in_first always 0 when active, which follows from being copy-phase only).
